Assembly: Lay the finished panel flat, WS facing up. Fold it in half so the two short edges meet at the top — the fold becomes the bottom of the bag. Pin the two open side edges together, matching row for row. Starting at the folded bottom and working up to the top opening, seam each side edge using mattress stitch or whip stitch (see Seaming Techniques). Weave in any remaining ends.

Border Round 1: With Colour 1, join yarn with sl st in the corner st of the last row at either side seam. Hold the bag right side out with the top opening toward you. Work in rounds without turning. The turning chain at the corner of the last row counts as a st. Ch 1 (does not count as a st). Starting in the same st as the join, *sc in each of next 4 sts, 2 sc in next st; rep from * 8 more times, sc in next st, working along the foundation edge into the base of each st of the first row, *sc in each of next 4 sts, 2 sc in next st; rep from * 8 more times, sc in next st. Join with sl st to first sc. (110 sts)
Border Round 2: Ch 1 (does not count as a st), sc in same st and in each of next 109 sts. Join with sl st to first sc. (110 sts)
Border Round 3: Ch 1 (does not count as a st), sc in same st and in each of next 109 sts. Join with sl st to first sc. (110 sts)

Handle Round: Each ch 56 below is a strap. The 25 sts skipped after each strap are its handle opening. Each strap chain should measure about 14 in flat. Chain loosely or go up a hook size if your chains run tight. Ch 1 (does not count as a st), sc in same st and in each of next 14 sts, ch 56 loosely, taking care not to twist the chain, skip next 25 sts, sc in each of next 30 sts, ch 56 loosely, taking care not to twist the chain, skip next 25 sts, sc in each of next 15 sts. Join with sl st to first sc. Fasten off. (60 sts, 112 ch)

Strap Round 1: With Colour 2, join yarn with sl st in the first st of the Handle Round. Work 1 sc in each ch of the straps. Each sc2tog joins a strap's end ch to the rim st beside it. Ch 1 (does not count as a st), sc in same st and in each of next 13 sts, sc2tog, sc in each of next 54 ch, sc2tog, sc in each of next 28 sts, sc2tog, sc in each of next 54 ch, sc2tog, sc in each of next 14 sts. Join with sl st to first sc. (168 sts)
Strap Round 2: Ch 1 (does not count as a st), sc in same st and in each of next 167 sts. Join with sl st to first sc. (168 sts)
Strap Round 3: Ch 1 (does not count as a st), sc in same st and in each of next 167 sts. Join with sl st to first sc. (168 sts)
Edging Round: Working left to right (do not turn), work reverse sc (crab st) in each of next 168 sts. Join with sl st to first st. Fasten off, weave in ends. (168 sts)

Handle 1 Edging: With Colour 1, join yarn with sl st in the first skipped st of handle opening 1. Work along the 25 skipped sts of the opening and then along the underside of the strap. Ch 1 (does not count as a st), sc in same st and in each of next 24 sts, sc in the free loop of each of the 56 ch. Join with sl st to first sc. Fasten off, weave in ends. (81 sts)

Handle 2 Edging: With Colour 1, join yarn with sl st in the first skipped st of handle opening 2. Work along the 25 skipped sts of the opening and then along the underside of the strap. Ch 1 (does not count as a st), sc in same st and in each of next 24 sts, sc in the free loop of each of the 56 ch. Join with sl st to first sc. Fasten off, weave in ends. (81 sts)

Reinforcing the Straps: Cut two lengths of twill tape, ribbon, or non-stretch interfacing, each 16 in long. Lay one along the underside of each strap, tuck 1 in at each end down inside the border, and sew it in place along both long edges and through the border, so the strap can't stretch under weight.

Pocket: Ch 24. Skip the first chain from the hook (it doesn't count as a stitch). Sc in the next chain and each ch across. Ch 1, turn. Work 11 more rows of sc (12 rows total). Fasten off. Sew the pocket to the front panel, centered 2 in below the border, leaving the top edge open as the pocket opening. (23 sts)

Adding a Zipper and Liner: Cut one piece of light-to-medium weight non-stretch fabric 15 in wide × 33.5 in long (bag width + 1 in side seam allowance; twice the bag height + 1.5 in top seam allowance, this bag being a flat panel with no gusset). Fold in half RIGHT SIDES together so the fold becomes the bottom of the liner, then sew up both open sides 0.5 in from the raw edge and fold the top raw edge under 0.75 in. Do not sew the liner into the bag by itself. Instead, with the liner wrong-side out and the zipper right side up, sandwich the zipper between the crochet's Border Round 3 (right side out, below the strap openings) and the liner's folded top edge, centering everything and tucking the zipper stopper-end tail in at a 90° angle so it won't show. Pin through all three layers together. Sew all the way around one side through the crochet and zipper only, dipping the needle into the fold of the liner for about 1/4 in along the way to hide the stitches on both the public side and inside the liner. Repeat on the opposite side.

Starting at the folded bottom and working up to the top opening, seam each side edge using mattress stitch or whip stitch (see Seaming Techniques). Weave in any remaining ends.

Top Band Round 1: Join yarn with sl st in the corner st of the last row at either side seam. Hold the bag right side out with the top opening toward you. Work in rounds without turning. The turning chain at the corner of the last row counts as a st. Ch 1 (does not count as a st). Starting in the same st as the join, sc in each of next 56 sts, working along the foundation edge into the base of each st of the first row, sc in each of next 56 sts. Join with sl st to first sc. (112 sts)
Top Band Round 2: Ch 2 (does not count as a st), hdc in same st and in each of next 111 sts. Join with sl st to first hdc. (112 sts)
Top Band Round 3: Ch 2 (does not count as a st), hdc in same st and in each of next 111 sts. Join with sl st to first hdc. Fasten off, weave in ends. (112 sts)

Attaching Handle 1: Attach this handle to the front panel, placing the ends approx 12 sts in from each side seam (approx 3 in) and approx 4 rows below the top band (approx 2 in), so the attachment sits on sturdier fabric instead of right at the edge. Sew each end down with a double row of whip stitch, stitching through that panel only — keep the front and back panels separate so the bag opening stays open.

Attaching Handle 2: Attach this handle to the back panel, placing the ends approx 12 sts in from each side seam (approx 3 in) and approx 4 rows below the top band (approx 2 in), so the attachment sits on sturdier fabric instead of right at the edge. Sew each end down with a double row of whip stitch, stitching through that panel only — keep the front and back panels separate so the bag opening stays open.

Pocket: Ch 29. Skip the first chain from the hook (it doesn't count as a stitch). Sc in the next chain and each ch across. Ch 1, turn. Work 9 more rows of sc (10 rows total). Fasten off. Sew the pocket to the front panel, centered 2 in below the top band, leaving the top edge open as the pocket opening. (28 sts)

Foundation: Ch 41.

Skip the first chain from the hook (it doesn't count as a stitch). Sc in the next chain and each ch across. Ch 1, turn. Work 5 more rows of sc (6 rows total). Fasten off. Fold the strip in half lengthwise (WS together) and whip stitch the long edges together for a doubled, reinforced strap. (40 sts)

Assembly: Lay the finished panel flat, WS facing up. Fold it in half so the two short edges meet at the top — the fold becomes the bottom of the bag. Pin the two open side edges together, matching row for row. Starting at the folded bottom and working up to the top opening, seam each side edge using mattress stitch or whip stitch (see Seaming Techniques). Weave in any remaining ends.

(112 sts)
